items.title: Frank Alkyer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 10, 2020
items.q: We wanted to get B.B. King and Les Paul together to do a conversation because they both had great respect for each other.

ctx.x: You know this is interesting, I rarely ask this question with musicians and I tried it a bunch of times, and the question was, “What’s the worst gig you ever played.” And I don’t know if anybody’s ever actually answered it. And if at all it usually isn’t something about the music, it’s more like the bus broke down — it’s a non-musical thing.

Right, right, right. Well for me there are things that didn’t happen. Things that we tried to do, all right — this is just, to this day, oh, things that didn’t happen. I loved Tito Puente. I got to spend time with him, got to know him, I loved his music before that, I loved it after that, I loved Tito Puente. And the timing of his death was such that it would have been great stress on the staff to put him on the cover, and putting him on the next cover would have been too far away. So it was just — and I wish…
You were mentioning about the cover with Tito Puente. How far ahead — when does your magazine have to be done?
